x: 7. · P.Duckett · Bels · 43.15

Carl Lawton led the boys home followed by Brian Ward with newcomer Paul Duckett breathing down his neck only ½ a minute down. Paul still has three years to go as a junior and on his present form there will be few to beat him in a year or two.
Paul Coates will have a good saason if he can get his leg right while our younger ranks have been growing apace with Paul Duckett and Andy Hinchcliff showing particular promise.

First Chamionship win for Wil Wesch, Bob Coates and Paul Duckett filling the minor placings. Wil's time was not as fast as usual "taking it easy" but Paul walked a stormer to come through strongly over the later stages.
The Olympic Cup was won by Carl Lawton from a fast improving Paul Duckett. Andy Hinchcliff( who has six more years in this championship) revenged an earlier defeat by Vic Butcher to finish fourth.

Perhaps a shadow of things to come, a strong Leicester outfit defeated the full Belgrave squad by six points and exposed our lack of a really top class speed merchant to provide the needle tip to the arrow. Behind the scoring four Bob Coates and Paul Duckett collected their badges for covering over 7 in the hour.

In the Junior '5' before the Metropolitan Walking Club 20 Kilos Paul Duckett returned a snappy 41.08 In the main race only Ray Middleton shone and Belgrave were pipped by a greatly improved Coventry team including ex-belgravian Bill Wright.
Nearly a clean sweep for Belgrave in the Surrey County Track Walks. The senior was won by Paul Nihill from Wil Wesch, Paul Duckett took the junior and Andy Hinchcliff walked off with the youth title.
Despite all of the aforementioned successes our lads had still not finished, and it was most refreshing to see those Pat Duncan coached youngsters Hinchcliffe (Youth) and P.

On the home front Paul Duckett and Andy Hinchcliff have both produced some good races in preperation for the winter with Paul's 24.50 for fourth place in the English Schools 5,000 Metres being a particularly creditable performance.
SHEEN GRAMMAR---Nigel Duckett clocked a record 28.5 in winning the 220 yards event against Garth on June 12th. He also has a 12.1 hundred and a 65.0 quarter to his credit.

Next season should see Arnold surging ahead again with his best of 6'-3" being regularly achieved. Our best performer of the day was undoubtedly Paul Duckett who finished 4th in the 5,000 metres walk with the good time of 24:50.
Our only other finalist was Paul Duckett who finished 6th in the 3,000 metres walk with a time of 14:52.2, but there were no qualifying races for this event.
Brian Ward, Gerry Cameron and Bob Picton all looked to be on the trail again and up north Dave King and Paul Duckett are sure to be slipping in some crafty sessions.
In the Junior Five Mile Race our only starter Paul Duckett banged in a useful 41.08. Paul is now at Manchester University and has already made his mark with our friends in Lancashire Walking Club.

However on October 19th, at Manchester, Carl Lawton, Brian Ward and Paul Duckett filled fourth team position. The winter season began well for Belgrave with Len Duquemin and the club taking top honours in the Highgate Open Seven.

Other Belgravians in the Surrey team were John Hamilton (54.2y) and Paul Duckett (7:35.8 mile walk). John Stow had the fastest lap of the day while representing his school in the annual Walton A.C. schools road relay on Oct. 25th.
Lack of competition did not prevent Paul Duckett from turning in a useful 42:12 to win this championship. Andy Hinchcliff, 3 years younger than Paul, took the silver medal and broke 47 minutes.

In the Junior the holder, Paul Duckett, was suprised to find the you police cadet Whitehead well ahead. This police boy, introduced by John Bromley could well turn in some useful performances in the future.
